I've farmed these 13.1 mu for 15 years, and I know what my family can handle. My wife works at a factory in town, so most days it's just me in the fields. I split the land into two parts: 10 mu for my wheat-maize rotation, and 3.1 mu for cotton.

Right now it's early spring, and my winter wheat needs attention. I'll topdress nitrogen when it greens up and again at jointing. With my well, I can irrigate three times through the season. Two pesticide sprays — one for weeds, one for diseases if they show up — should keep it clean. I expect around 460 kg/mu if the weather holds.

Come June, right after wheat harvest, I'll rotary-till that same 10 mu and plant hybrid summer maize. Maize grows fast and doesn't need as much babysitting as cotton. I'll side-dress urea at jointing, irrigate twice, and spray twice. I usually get about 560 kg/mu.

My cotton goes in late April on the 3.1 mu plot. Cotton is picky — it needs plenty of potash and regular spraying for bollworm. I'll rotary-till in spring, put down compound fertilizer, and stay on top of the pests with five applications. I'll irrigate three times during flowering and boll development. I know this variety well; it should give me about 85 kg/mu of seed cotton.

I don't chase new fads. My wife's salary covers our child's school fees, so I farm steady — stick to what I know, don't gamble on strange seeds, and keep the well pump maintained. That's how I'll manage this year.
